reason: The sponsor-loaded tablet is the centre of the request desk, but it is not clear whether the listening app needs removal or another change first.
expectation: Inspection should show which available item can help prepare the tablet.

alternatives.reason: The screwdriver might open the tablet, but the problem described is an app rather than an obvious hardware fault.

effect: The listening app is removed and the microphone disconnected, leaving the tablet ready to become a deliberate-use request desk.
reaction: The physical disconnection makes the privacy change reassuringly visible.
reason: The large request button looks like a practical way to make the tablet's request form accessible.
expectation: The button will be fitted to the tablet as a way to initiate a request.

effect: The large request button currently has no available combination, so I need to prepare something else first.
reaction: I was surprised the button could not yet be fitted.
reason: Inspecting the modified tablet should reveal its available next step without guessing among the remaining desk parts.
expectation: The inspection will identify what can currently be combined with the tablet.

effect: The tablet now uses the local controller and has its outside network route blocked; the remaining desk parts may now be usable.
reaction: Keeping requests local makes the privacy change more concrete.
reason: Now that the request form is connected locally, the large button may be ready to provide deliberate access.
expectation: The button will be fitted to the local request tablet.

effect: The locally connected tablet now has a deliberate press-to-send button.
reaction: The distinction between sending a request and listening to nearby conversation is satisfying.
reason: The screen hood should help give people privacy while they use the request desk.
expectation: The hood will fit around the tablet screen.

effect: The hood shields the request form from people waiting in the queue.
reaction: A simple cardboard privacy screen is a satisfying fit.
reason: The old receipt printer may give requesters a record of what they submit.
expectation: The printer will connect to the request tablet to provide receipts.

effect: The printer connects to the local controller rather than the tablet, providing receipts while keeping return details off the shared queue.
reaction: The compatibility feedback clarified the connection, and the privacy controls are useful.
reason: The local queue printer and shielded request tablet appear to be the two prepared parts of the request desk.
expectation: The printer and tablet will form a usable local request desk.

effect: The tablet and printer now form a private request desk, with a pencil and paper option.
reaction: The non-digital option makes the desk feel more inclusive.
reason: Moth is the remaining relevant component, and its source and correction controls may help make the request desk usable.

choice.combine: Moth with source display and correction controls

expectation: Moth will connect its correction controls to the request desk.

effect: Moth's help is optional, and users can review its suggested wording or keep their own; the request desk goal is complete.
reaction: Sal keeping her original wording was a nice demonstration of user control.

mostWorthwhile.text: Connecting the printer to the local controller was worthwhile: it provided receipts while keeping return details off the shared queue and exposing deletion controls.

leastWorthwhile.text: My first button attempt was unproductive because the tablet had to be connected locally first; that dependency was not obvious to me.

surprise.text: I expected the printer to connect directly to the tablet, but it instead connected to the local controller automatically.

arbitrary.text: The required order for fitting the button initially felt unclear, although connecting the form locally first made sense once revealed.

continue.text: Yes. I would be interested to see how the locally controlled infrastructure develops; the privacy choices and optional assistance were more engaging than simply assembling the desk.
